finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize, so the authorization check is not enforced. Any caller can run DROP TABLE. The table name is also concatenated into SQL, which allows injection.
finding.source: HTTP request to /admin/drop by any user, including one without the 'dba' role. The 't' form value is attacker-controlled.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered to dropTable with no auth middleware
userFrom(r) takes the user from the request context
Authorize returns errors.New("forbidden") for non-dba users, but the return value is discarded
The unvalidated form value is concatenated into the SQL string and executed

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its result is not checked, so it has no effect. Compare vacuum at api.go:33-36, which does check it. No other middleware or validation is applied to the route. The table name is not allowlisted or quoted. Auth middleware that sets the context 'user' is not in this code. userFrom does an unchecked type assertion, so a request with no user in the context panics, but that is only a DoS and net/http recovers from the panic.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is called but its error return is discarded; no middleware on the route (api.go:44), no allowlist, quoting or parameterization of the table name.
verdict.reason: api.go:26 discards Authorize's error, so any user whose request carries a user in context reaches api.go:27, where the unvalidated r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into DROP TABLE; vacuum at api.go:33 shows the correct check.
